summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A)

## BOOK 1 of 2: STRONG POISON (Dorothy L. Sayers, 1930; Gutenberg 78157)

Epigraph: old ballad "Lord Rendal" ("Where gat ye your dinner...", "Oh that was strong poison...").

**Characters (Book 1):**
- Harriet Vane: accused, 29, mystery novelist, dark smudgy eyes, square brows; tried for murder of Philip Boyes by arsenic. Bought arsenic 10 Apr 1928-cited as 10 April (Southampton Row, chemist Mr. Brown, signed "Mary Slater") and 5 May (weed-killer, signed "Edith Waters"); also prussic acid, strychnine, attempted aconitine. Lived Doughty Street, No. 100 flat (above Mrs. Bright). Publisher: Mr. Trufoot. Agent: Mr. Challoner. Novel in progress: "Death in the Pot".
- Philip Boyes: 36, writer (5 novels), "advanced" views; lover of Harriet from March 1928; quarrel Feb 1929 (marriage proposal, she felt "made a fool of"). Father: Rev. Arthur Boyes, vicar of Tweedling Parva. Cousin: Norman Urquhart (solicitor, Woburn Square, Bedford Row office). Letter to Harriet 16 June 1929 ("Dear Harriet... I shall be in town on the 20th"); her reply "Dear Phil ... 9.30 on the 20th".
- Sir Impey Biggs: defence counsel. Mr. Crofts (Crofts & Cooper, solicitors). Attorney-General. Judge (old, parrot-faced; later Bancroft mentioned as next judge; Crossley mentioned).
- Lord Peter Wimsey (amateur detective, monocle, valet Bunter). Freddy Arbuthnot (Hon. Freddy). Dowager Duchess of Denver (Wimsey's mother). Chief-Inspector Charles Parker. Miss Katharine Climpson (typing bureau "the Cattery"; juror, elderly spinster).
- Witnesses/others: Sylvia Marriott, Eiluned Price (Harriet's friends); Ryland Vaughan (Boyes' friend, Harlech); Dr. Grainger, Dr. Weare (doctors); Nurse Williams; Hannah Westlock (maid at Urquhart house); Mrs. Pettican (cook); Mr. Brown (chemist); Burke (taxi-driver, Guilford Street); PC D.1234; Mrs. Bright; Mrs. Bulfinch (formerly Gracie Montague, barmaid at the Nine Rings, Grays Inn Road); Mrs. Wrayburn/Cremorna Garden (actress, great-aunt); Marjorie Phelps (figurine maker); Kropotkys; Joey Trimbles; Bill Rumm ("Blindfold Bill", ex-burglar, now locksmith, Whitechapel Rd; wife Bella; daughter Esmeralda Hyacinth); Joan Murchison (Miss Murchison, Cattery typist planted at Urquhart's office); Mr. Pond (head clerk); Mrs. Hodges (charwoman); Miss Booth (Caroline Booth, nurse); Mrs. Craig (medium); Mrs. Pegler, Miss Tweall, Miss Etheredge, Mrs. Liffey (boarding house, Windle); Pongo (control); Mr. Cole (Grimsby & Cole, publishers); Mr. Pritchard; Sir James Lubbock (analyst); Mrs. Rushworth (party); Naomi Rushworth (later engaged to Penberthy); Nellie (housemaid); Mrs. Mitcham (housekeeper).

**Key events (Book 1):**
- Trial at Old Bailey; jury deadlocks after ~6.5 hours; discharged; Miss Climpson held out.
- Timeline of Boyes' death: dinner at Norman Urquhart's, 8 pm (sherry Oloroso 1847, bouillon, turbot, poulet en casserole, omelette made by Boyes from eggs Urquhart cracked-one; Corton burgundy drunk only by Boyes, later analysed harmless). Left Doughty St 9.15/9.25 arrival 9.25; taxi at Guilford Street 10.10; arrived Woburn Sq. ill; died 3 am 23 June. Dr. Grainger diagnosed gastritis. Exhumation later. Analysis: ~4-5 grains arsenic. No indigo/charcoal traces.
- Hair arsenic near roots indicated ~10 weeks prior exposure.
- Boyes' dying words: "Harriet'll be rid of me now."
- Wimsey visits Harriet in Holloway; proposes; she refuses ("forty-seven proposals").
- Wimsey investigates: Mrs. Bulfinch's story (Nine Rings pub, Grays Inn Road, c. 20-21 June, ~10.05 pm, man drank water with white powder from paper packet; packet later left behind, found by Parker's men in pub—found to be bicarbonate of soda at the end, or rather the packet found was bicarbonate of soda).
- Mrs. Wrayburn's will: real will (5 June 1920) leaves Boyes real estate + £50,000; Urquhart residuary + executor; draft shown by Urquhart falsified.
- Urquhart's embezzlement from Mrs. Wrayburn's estate via Megatherium Trust (Miss Murchison's discovery).
- Miss Murchison (Cattery) picks locks (taught by Bill Rumm); finds Deed of Trust, letter; later finds hidden panel with secret share papers and white packet of arsenic in Urquhart's office.
- Marsh's test at Wimsey's flat: arsenic confirmed. Wimsey realizes arsenic taken earlier and via omelette trick? Final solution: Urquhart ("Oliver"? no—that's Book 2) had immunized himself to arsenic (Styrian method, eating small amounts) and dosed the omelette egg (cracked egg); confessed when Wimsey tricked him (Wimsey claimed he'd eaten arsenical sugar/Turkish delight); Urquhart tried to escape, caught by Parker; "Mithridates" line.
- Miss Climpson's Windle investigation: boarding house Hillside View; nurse Caroline Booth; séances with Ouija/table rapping; obtained will from Mrs. Wrayburn's safe (combination found via "B" message and black note-book numbers 12,18,4,0,9,3,15); letter to Norman Urquhart; soap-box cracking fake.
- Manicurist (Bunter/Wimsey) gets hair/nail clippings of Urquhart.
- Ending: Crown withdraws charge; Harriet acquitted; Wimsey says he'll marry her ("If she'll have me").

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE UNPLEASANTNESS AT THE BELLONA CLUB (Dorothy L. Sayers, 1928; Gutenberg 72855)

Chapters I–XXIII (Chapter titles given as italic phrases, e.g., "Old Mossy-face", "Hearts Count More Than Diamonds", "Lord Peter Forces A Card", etc.).

**Characters (Book 2):**
- General Arthur Fentiman ("Old Mossy-face"), ~90, grandfather of George and Robert; Crimea, Majuba veteran; Bellona Club arm-chair by fire; found dead 11 Nov 1928? (Armistice Day, body found ~7 pm, rigid; left knee-joint loose). Former residence: Dover Street flat; manservant Woodward.
- Captain George Fentiman (gassed WWI, shell-shock, nervy; wife Sheila; flat in Finsbury Park; landlady Mrs. Munns, charlady Mrs. Crickett; debt to Dougal MacStewart (money-lender); later job at Walmisley-Hubbard car firm; shadowed by a sleuth; found in Clerkenwell after confessing in delirium).
- Major Robert Fentiman (elder brother, army, lives in Richmond; executor & residuary legatee; staged the death concealment; later absconded to France/Italy with "Oliver" trick; struck by Wimsey, later dies? — no: he disappears; in the end flees).
- Sheila Fentiman (George's wife; ran tea-shop in Kensington).
- Lady Felicity Dormer (General's sister; Victorian elopement with button-maker Henry Dormer; died 10:37 am 11 Nov); ward Miss Ann Dorland (painter, Chelsea, plain, dark bob, heir; ex-lover Ambrose Ledbury; engaged secretly to Dr. Penberthy).
- Dr. Walter Penberthy (Army surgeon, Harley Street; certified death; glands/rejuvenation enthusiast; poisoned General with digitalin in capsules/pill; later engaged to Naomi Rushworth; shot himself in Bellona library after confessing in written statement).
- Mr. Murbles (family solicitor, Staple Inn; soda-mint lozenges; "Mr. Murbles" hates Pritchard).
- Mr. Pritchard (Lady Dormer's man of business, Lincoln's Inn).
- Colonel Marchbanks (Bellona Club; gave Penberthy his loaded revolver).
- Wetheridge (Club grumbler); Culyer (Club Secretary); Rogers (commissionaire); Weston (new assistant commissionaire); Williamson (cloakroom attendant); Piper (hall-porter); Babcock (wine steward); Tin-Tummy Challoner; Fred (waiter); Dick Challoner; Ormsby.
- Mr. Oliver (mysterious man who telephoned Woodward at ~9 pm on 10 Nov claiming General was staying with him; real/invented; "Oliver Twist" book clue; Charing Cross call box; "Paris" sleuth letter was a decoy by Wimsey).
- Sleuths Incorporated (detective agency); Chief-Inspector Parker; Sir James Lubbock (analyst) and Saunders; Dr. Horner; Nurse Armstrong; Nellie (housemaid); Mrs. Mitcham (housekeeper); Nurse Williams? (no, that's Book 1).
- Taxi drivers Swain and Hinkins (saw General to Penberthy's, then to Bellona via Regent's Park, dropping George at Gloucester Gate).
- Joan Murchison (typist at Urquhart's? — no, that's Book 1 character; in Book 2 she is a Cattery secretary who wrote letter about Megatherium Trust, employed by Mr. Urquhart? —— Note: In Book 2, Miss Murchison (Joan) is the Cattery clerk who wrote letter re Megatherium; she ARE later... (Note: the Book 2 text "Joan Murchison" letter about Megatherium Trust is in Book 2's chapter XI? — Not present; it's Book 1's Urquhart). **Correction**: Book 2 contains Joan Murchison's letter in Chapter XI re Mr. Urquhart at Bedford Row; she is a Cattery clerk placed at Urquhart's office. Urquhart is a Book-2 character too (Norman Urquhart, Megatherium Trust, Mrs. Wrayburn)? — In Book 2, the Bedford Row solicitor is Norman Urquhart as in Book 1? It is in Book 2 (Chapter XI–XIV) referenced Urquhart as "Mr. Urquhart", Bedford Row, Megatherium Trust, deed-box WRAYBURN, secret panel; Miss Murchison. (Same characters as Book 1, reused.)
- Ann Dorland ("Miss Dorland") — inheritor; in book 2, eventually arrested, released; married? Note: she eventually declines to be arrested; later at the trial? (Not reached.)
- Mrs. Pettican & Hannah Westlock (Book 1 only). Bunter (Wimsey's valet; photographer; "Bunter's crumpets").

**Key events (Book 2):**
- Armistice Day, 11 Nov: Gen. Fentiman found dead in Bellona smoking-room arm-chair ~7 pm (Wimsey present; Fentiman laughed hysterically "We're all dead..."). Dr. Penberthy certifies. Lady Dormer dies 10:37 am same day.
- Telephone in ante-room cabinet marked "Out of Order" (Wetheridge complaint) — used to hide body.
- Woodward (General's man): General left flat 9:45 am 10 Nov? (Woodward says ~9:45/10 am). Visited Lady Dormer's at ~3 pm 10 Nov (phone call from Portman Square), went to Harley Street ~4:30 by taxi (Swain), Penberthy gave digitalin; then taxi to Bellona ~6:40 pm (Hinkins), George dropped at Gloucester Gate; Robert found General dead ~8 pm in library, moved to telephone cabinet, then to arm-chair ~ midnight; "Oliver" phone call at 9:13 pm from Charing Cross box.
- Wimsey's investigation: photographs by Bunter; fingerprints on stick; varnish on boot; corpses' leg; notes in General's hand (library notes: R £150,000, G £300,000...); exhumation applied (Robert), Penberthy's statement; Lubbock analysis: digitalin; Home Office.
- Robert arrested? Not — Robert absconds; Wimsey pursues decoy "Paris" trip; confrontation; George confesses in delirium; Robert struck by Wimsey (Ch XVIII-XIX); Penberthy's written confession, suicide in Bellona library (with Colonel Marchbanks' revolver); George found in Clerkenwell.
- Final: Penberthy suicide; Ann Dorland released; Robert resigned from Army; George recovers.

Notes for Q&A: Book 2 ends with Wetheridge complaining of corked wine at the Bellona.
